A continuing study and a series of English production will give us the "other side of the question."

Laboratories.—The College maintained a laboratory with "sufficient Chemical and Philosophical apparatus to illustrate any of the principles usually taught in any college textbook," according to its advertising as early as 1883. It is recalled by ex-students that the department of anatomy and physiology was accompanied by dissection in which the students in the course were required to be able to assemble in its entirety, identifying each bone by name, and that dissection of animals for laboratory demonstrations was common. An original copy of the laboratory note book paper refers to the College laboratory's being thoroughly decorated and "put in order" by October 1, 1884, which would seem to indicate that the laboratory had been in use for some time previous.

The Administrative Organization and Polity of the College.

    Ownership and Ownership.—Although the charter of the College sets out that the College was sold for a hundred fifty shares and names the five incorporators, no records have been found to trace the precise nature of the financial interest in the corporation or that the title to the College properties remained in these proprietors. It is probable that such a transaction as that implied in the deed from F. J. Abernathy in 1876, referred to in Chapter III, and the retention of the management and conduct of the affairs of the institution seems to have been retained in President Halsell throughout the school's existence.
